feedback.problem: Consider a square such that its area $A$ can vary. What is the best interpretation of ${s}^{′}(A)$ if $s$ is the length of each side of the square?
feedback.worked_solution:
The function $s(A)$ gives the length of each side of a square with area $A.$ So,

$$
{s}^{′}(A)=\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}A}=\frac{\text{Change in }s}{\text{Change in }A}.
$$

Therefore, ${s}^{′}(A)$ is the rate at which each side changes as the area changes.

submitted_fields.submitted_value: The rate at which each side changes as the area changes
